newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes slighty weaker in modest trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes slighty weaker in modest trading.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes were slightly weaker Monday morning in sluggish activitiy to start the week.

Cash dealers said domestic grade differentials and Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) were talked at steady price levels, though most grades were actually holding onto weak trading levels established the later stages of last week.

July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was 10 cents lower at $18.85-95 a barrel, tracking the weaker stance taken by NYMEX futures this morning. Added to the July NYMEX price was the 20 cents premium from the July EFP market, traders said.
"The EFPs are at 18-22 cents over the paper. There haven't been any new trades but we're talked at those levels," said a cash trader in Texas.
August EFPs were also marking premiums of around 10 cents to the August NYMEX contract.
On the grade front, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was pegged at 20-25 cents under the cash benchmark WTI/Cushing, steady from last deals recorded on Friday.

Arbitrage for bringing over North Sea Brent barrels to the U.S. Gulf remained wide around $1.60, figuring the $1.10 spread between July WTI/Brent off screens and the minus 50 cents being paid for Dated Brent cargoes.
Sour barrels extended the bearish tone set last week, talked around a $2.00 discount for Eugene Island barrels and from $1.67--73 under for the West Texas Sour/Midland market.
"Of all the crudes out there to buy, the sours are the most plentiful in supply," said a cash dealer.
Talk of more economical Venezuelan grades and a slew of other supply deflated the sours, the trading source added.
July WTI/Cushing Postings Plus were measured at $1.77-83.
